title: Adaptive Model Pricing & Fidelity API design spec
author: Aisha Karim
content:
Overview

Purpose: This design spec defines the Adaptive Model Pricing & Fidelity API — a server-side API and contract that enables per-request fidelity negotiation between customer SDKs/agents and Redwood serving components. The goal is to let runtime and billing systems jointly select an output fidelity level that meets latency and quality SLOs while respecting customer budget and pricing rules.

Audience: product managers, serving runtime engineers, billing, SDK teams, security.

Background and motivation
- Customers have diverse requirements: some prioritize cost and can tolerate lower fidelity; others need consistent high-quality outputs for critical paths.
- Current switches (static fidelity per-route or tenant) are coarse and require manual pricing changes or feature flags.
- We need an automated, observable negotiation layer that:
  - Chooses fidelity per-request or per-session,
  - Exposes easy hooks for customer budget constraints, per-route SLOs, and billing signals, and
  - Produces deterministic billing attribution and audit logs.

Goals
1) Define a small, extensible API for fidelity negotiation used by SDKs and internal routing services.
2) Specify the scoring and decision inputs so different runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private) make consistent choices.
3) Ensure decisions are auditable and billable with stable identifiers.
4) Provide fallback paths when negotiation fails (offline, timeout, incompatible client).

Non-goals
- Full implementation of pricing engine (this spec defines interfaces and decision points, not every pricing model).
- Replacing existing long-term contract billing flows; integration points only.

Stakeholders and owners
- Product owner: Aisha Karim (product)
- Runtime integration: Serving Runtime team (owner: Evan Liu)
- Billing & metering: Finance & Billing (owner: María González)
- SDKs & client: DevX SDK team (owner: Jonah Reed)
- Security review: Security team

Glossary
- Fidelity level: an integer label (e.g., high, medium, low) representing model/variant tradeoffs (latency/cost/quality).
- Pricing signal: information used by pricing engine (per-token cost, per-request surcharge, credits).
- Negotiation context: set of inputs (route, tenant, SLOs, budget) for a decision.

API surface
- Base path: POST /v1/fidelity/negotiate
- Auth: standard Redwood API Key header (Authorization: Bearer <token>)
- Timeout: 80ms by default for negotiation (configurable per-tenant).

Request schema (JSON) — fields that SDKs and internal routers MUST provide where available:
{
  "client_request_id": "string, recommended",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "route": "string, e.g., /v1/generate or custom route id",
  "latency_slo_ms": "int, optional p95 target in ms",
  "max_cost_usd": "number, optional per-request budget cap",
  "quality_profile": "string enum [strict, balanced, lenient]",
  "context_statistics": "object, optional: recent avg tokens, prefix cache hit rate",
  "candidate_variants": ["list of variant ids with metadata, optional"]
}

Response schema (JSON)
{
  "decision_id": "stable string id for auditing",
  "selected_variant_id": "string",
  "fidelity_tier": "string enum [high, medium, low]",
  "estimated_latency_ms": "int",
  "estimated_cost_usd": "number",
  "reason_codes": ["list of short reasons: SLO_MATCH, BUDGET_CAP, FALLBACK_TO_ROUTE_DEFAULT"],
  "trace_link": "string (optional link to trace in console)",
  "ttl_seconds": "int, how long decision can be cached client-side"
}

Example request
POST /v1/fidelity/negotiate
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "client_request_id": "req-20270330-9x3",
  "tenant_id": "acme-inc",
  "route": "customer-chat",
  "latency_slo_ms": 120,
  "max_cost_usd": 0.0025,
  "quality_profile": "balanced",
  "context_statistics": {"avg_input_tokens": 110, "cache_prefix_hit_rate": 0.45}
}

Example response
{
  "decision_id": "dec-20270330-001",
  "selected_variant_id": "gptx-medium-q4",
  "fidelity_tier": "medium",
  "estimated_latency_ms": 98,
  "estimated_cost_usd": 0.0019,
  "reason_codes": ["SLO_MATCH", "COST_WITHIN_BUDGET"],
  "trace_link": "https://console.redwood.internal/traces/dec-20270330-001",
  "ttl_seconds": 60
}

Fidelity tiers and pricing signals (recommended defaults)
| fidelity_tier | example_variant | p95_latency_ms | est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | quality_profile_match | notes |
|---------------|-----------------|----------------|----------------------------|------------------------|-------|
| high          | gptx-large-q8   | 250            | 0.020                      | strict                 | high-quality, high-cost |
| medium        | gptx-medium-q4  | 90             | 0.007                      | balanced               | default for most routes|
| low           | gptx-small-q2   | 40             | 0.002                      | lenient                | for bulk/background jobs |

Decision logic (high-level)
1) Validate inputs and tenant policy (deny if tenant policy forbids negotiation).
2) Filter candidate variants by compatibility (model supports requested features).
3) Score candidates by normalized cost and latency match to requested latency_slo_ms and max_cost_usd. Score formula (simplified):
   score = w_latency * latency_score + w_cost * (1 - cost_scale) + w_quality * quality_score
   where default weights: w_latency=0.45, w_cost=0.35, w_quality=0.20.
4) Apply hard constraints: if estimated_cost > max_cost_usd then mark as ineligible.
5) Select highest scoring candidate; if none eligible, return route default with reason FALLBACK_ROUTE_DEFAULT.
6) Produce decision_id and attach deterministic metadata (tenant, route, inputs) for billing and audit.

Scoring operational notes
- latency_score is 1.0 if estimated_latency <= latency_slo_ms, otherwise decays by (estimated_latency - slo)/slo clipped at 0.
- cost_scale normalizes est_cost to a 0..1 range using tenant historical median per-token cost.
- quality_score is derived from offline evals per variant and quality_profile mapping.

Telemetry and metrics (required)
- fidelity.negotiation.requests - counter, labels: tenant_id, route, outcome (selected, fallback, timeout)
- fidelity.negotiation.latency_ms - histogram/p95 for negotiation duration
- fidelity.decision.selected_variant - counter labeled by variant_id, fidelity_tier, reason_code
- billing.decision.estimated_cost_usd - gauge (sampled) per decision id
- trace and link: decisions must include a trace id that links to request routing and final model request.

SLOs for the negotiation service
- Availability: 99.95% global (rolling 30d)
- P95 latency: <= 60ms (target)
- Failure mode: on timeouts (> timeout threshold) return immediate FALLBACK_ROUTE_DEFAULT with reason TIMEOUT and log decision telemetry.

Rollout plan and flags
Phase 0 (alpha, internal tenants)
- Feature flag: feature.adaptive_pricing.enabled = false by default
- Only SDKs from DevX internal builds call the API.
- Monitor negotiation outcomes and compare to existing static routing decisions.

Phase 1 (canary)
- Enable for 5% traffic for tenants in staging group.
- Compare cost and quality delta: require no >5% regression in quality metrics for high-priority routes.

Phase 2 (public opt-in)
- Self-serve toggle in Console per-tenant with default off.
- Billing disclaimer and sample cost simulator must be shown.

Phase 3 (on by default for selected product tiers)
- Documentation updates, SDK release, and channel communications.

Rollout steps (detailed)
1) Implement endpoint and add feature flag gate.
2) Deploy telemetry and dashboard (negotiation outcomes, avg cost delta by tenant).
3) Release SDK support for negotiation (vX with opt-in flag), include sample code.
4) Run internal canary tests with synthetic workloads (detailed in testing plan).
5) Gradual ramp following success criteria.

Backwards compatibility and migration
- If client does not call negotiate, route defaults remain unchanged.
- Decision ttl_seconds is advisory; SDKs may cache decisions but must refresh when route or tenant policy changes.
- Variant ids must remain stable; deprecations require 30-day notice and migration mapping.

Security and privacy
- Decisions contain tenant_id and route info — mark decision payloads PII-free but treat as customer-sensitive metadata.
- Audit logs retained per retention policy (Billing: 7 years; operational telemetry: 90 days).
- Ensure API access requires scoped API keys and tenant authorization checks.

Observability and debugging playbook
- When fidelity decisions produce unexpectedly lower quality:
  1) Inspect negotiation.trace_link and decision metadata.
  2) Validate offline eval scores for selected_variant_id.
  3) Compare against recent routing vs. static-routed results in A/B.
  4) If systemic, rollback feature flag and open bug with serving/runtime teams.

Testing matrix (minimum)
- Unit tests for scoring logic and cost normalization.
- Integration tests: negotiation -> routing -> model request.
- Chaos tests: simulate slow negotiation service; ensure fallback path triggers.
- Billing validation tests that decision_id maps to invoiceable events.

Configuration table (defaults)
- negotiation.timeout_ms: 80
- negotiation.default_weights: {"w_latency": 0.45, "w_cost":0.35, "w_quality":0.20} (config per-tenant override allowed)
- negotiation.ttl_seconds_default: 60
- negotiation.max_response_size: 2KB (decision payload)

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Should the negotiation endpoint return multiple candidate variants with ranked pass/fail so SDKs can choose local heuristics? (Pro: more client control. Con: increased complexity and audit surface.)
- Billing attribution granularity: per-decision vs per-model-request. Recommendation: emit both decision and final model request events and reconcile in billing pipeline.

Next steps and action items
- [Product] finalize API contract and sign-off on weights and default thresholds (owner: Aisha) — due 2027-04-05.
- [Runtime] prototype scoring service and integration hooks (owner: Evan) — due 2027-05-01.
- [Billing] define invoice mapping and retention for decisions (owner: María) — due 2027-05-10.
- [DevX] release SDK preview with negotiation support (owner: Jonah) — due 2027-05-20.

Appendix: sample SDK usage (pseudocode)
// pseudocode: negotiate then call generate
let decision = POST('/v1/fidelity/negotiate', {tenant_id, route, latency_slo_ms, max_cost_usd})
if (decision.fidelity_tier == 'low' && route.is_critical) {
  // optional override if client insists on higher fidelity
  use_variant('gptx-medium-q4')
} else {
  callGenerate(endpointForVariant(decision.selected_variant_id), payload)
}
